title: Exterior powers commute with module stalks
statement: For a scheme X [def-pc-scheme], a module sheaf M and n≥0, form its exterior sheaf [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. For every x in X, there is an O_{X,x}-linear equivalence (exteriorSheaf M n)_x ≃ exteriorPower n M_x, using stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. For every neighborhood U of x and tuple a in M(U), it sends the germ of exteriorSheafSection M n U a to the wedge of the germs of the entries of a.

source.place: Proof of (*), determinant paragraph: quotient lift independence; stalk algebra portion of lem-sc-exterior-tensor-kernel-locally-spanned

proof.text: Use the alternating wedge-germ map of lem-sc-exterior-presheaf-stalk-wedge and the exterior-power universal property to construct a linear map q from the exterior power of M_x to the stalk of the upstream sectionwise exterior presheaf. Construct the reverse additive map p by the stalk colimit universal property, sending section tuples to wedges of their germs on each neighborhood. Naturality follows on wedge generators and then by span induction, with scalars restricted along the section ring maps. The germ scalar formula makes p linear. The two composites are identities by span induction; in the stalk exterior power represent a finite tuple on a common neighborhood. This yields the presheaf comparison and its wedge-germ formula.

The sheafification unit induces an isomorphism of additive stalks by lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space. Represent a scalar and a section on a common neighborhood and apply the germ scalar formula to see this isomorphism is linear. Compose its inverse with the previous comparison. On wedge germs this gives exactly the stated formula. Empty tuples for n=0 and zero stalk rings require no exclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem exteriorSheaf_stalk_comparison {X : Scheme.{v}} (M : X.Modules)
    (n : ℕ) (x : X) :
    ∃ e : (exteriorPower M n).presheaf.stalk x ≃ₗ[X.presheaf.stalk x]
        ⋀[X.presheaf.stalk x]^n (M.presheaf.stalk x),
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) (a : Fin n → M.val.obj (op U)),
        e ((exteriorPower M n).presheaf.germ U x hx (wedge (M := M) (r := n) (U := U) a)) =
          exteriorPower.ιMulti (X.presheaf.stalk x) n
            (fun i ↦ M.presheaf.germ U x hx (a i))
lean.note: Retired the Sheaf copy in favor of the proved upstream theorem. The upstream theorem uses exteriorPower and wedge. In the sole consumer ExteriorTensorStalkKernelSpan, the private retainedExteriorSheaf_stalk_comparison identifies exteriorSheafPresheaf with the upstream exterior presheaf by an identity-on-sections isomorphism, sheafifies it, and uses unit naturality to identify wedge sections. Its linear stalk equivalence transports the upstream theorem to the retained exteriorSheaf API without any new hypothesis or hole.
